evidence.notes:
Caveats: c7 sidebar count stale until reload; c16 workers committed in each repository's own checkout after the approval rule denied /tmp worktrees; c4 needed a hand edit of the scratch project.json; c13 used an optional ticket accepted after the node.

## Discoveries

- **Sidebar count after Rescan** (DM-351): the sidebar row reads the project once per mount, so its repository count is stale after Rescan until a reload.
- **Validation lists missing repositories as choices** (DM-348): the `missing_repo` message names repositories a rescan marked missing.
- **An optional ticket accepted after the acceptance node** (DM-356, DM-357, DM-358): it adds a touched repository the node's increments did not name, so `increment_merged` and `definition_of_done` become unmet, and an accepted node cannot be claimed again in the run. Not exercised past the gate.
- **Touched repositories are read from the epic's active or latest run** (DM-355, DM-358), not from the run being evaluated.
- **Packet path vs `gitFor` path** (DM-355): the packet joins the project root and the name, while `gitFor` resolves real paths; they differ behind a symlinked root.
- **Where orchestrator agents put worktrees** (c16): the live agent asked for worker and integration worktrees under `/tmp`; the guides could name a location next to the folder so a scratch-only approval policy does not push workers into the child checkout.
- **`multi_repo` on an already set-up single repository** (DM-346): returns the existing project with no error saying the layout was ignored.
- **First-run kickoff** (DM-360): repository branches are bound at `start_run`, after the kickoff is sent, so a first-run kickoff lists only the epic branch.
- **Panel grouping** (DM-362): the acceptance panel groups Definition of Done rows by targeted repositories; the gate uses repositories with accepted tickets.

wentPoorly: DM-345 used three attempts: the orchestrator read the claim token from the wrong response field twice and then lost the third token in a kernel restart; the third attempt was reconciled with resubmit after its lease expired.

Per-ticket checks never ran the build or deadcode, so the combined sweep found a renderer build break (DM-361 imported core/schemas, which pulls node:crypto) and ~140 deadcode findings (DM-348 imported portable.ts into graph.ts, which the renderer imports).
Coverage fell below the 95% branch threshold on the combined work (94.97%) and needed a tests-only fix before landing; a DM-356 test also timed out under coverage on a loaded machine.
DM-356 changed the submit_attempt schema without updating the pinned fingerprint in src/mcp/validation.test.ts; neither its worker nor its reviewer ran that file.
The live check (c16) showed agents committing in a child repository's own checkout when the worktree location they wanted was denied.
wentWell: All 19 work tickets were accepted, 17 on their first attempt, with independent reviewers re-running each ticket's targeted checks.
Row checks caught a stale schema fingerprint (row 6) before the acceptance round, and merge conflicts (workspace.ts, testContext.ts) were additive and resolved at merge time.
Reviewers caught two single-repository regressions (DM-361 dialog gated on getProject; DM-362 report field shape) and each was fixed on the second attempt.
The acceptance round verified every covered item on scratch fixtures, including a live Claude Code orchestrator run from the built app.

risks: Schema migration V12 (epics.repository_branches_json) is on multi-repo-folders; other open epics that add a migration need renumbering when they merge to main.
A folder of repositories has no branch guard; the guides forbid switching a child checkout, but the live run (c16) shows an agent will do it when its preferred worktree location is denied.
An optional ticket accepted after the acceptance node can leave the increment and Definition of Done gates unmet with no way to re-claim the node (seen in a scratch run, not fixed).
Coverage clears the 95% branch threshold by 0.18 points; the multi-repository code still has about 40 untested branches, most judged unreachable.
The orchestrator fixed integration problems on the sprint branch (build, deadcode, coverage, a schema fingerprint); they were not reviewed by a separate reviewer.
